TASK ID: vertex-cover-to-set-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Set Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = SetCover
Set Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff AT MOST k of the sets together contain every element of the
universe.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. u = 0 is yes for every k >= 0 (choosing
no sets covers the empty universe). If some element is in no set, the
answer is no.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-qzgpix52

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-qzgpix52 && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover.

Vertex Cover instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
Set Cover instance:     {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}

Reduction: the universe is the set of edges (edge i corresponds to element i).
For every vertex v we create one set containing the indices of all edges
incident to v.  A collection of vertex-sets covers the universe iff the
corresponding vertices touch every edge, i.e. form a vertex cover.  Hence the
minimum set cover size equals the minimum vertex cover size, so the answer is
preserved for the same k.

Edge cases:
  * k < 0: both problems answer no (SetCover.is_yes returns False for k < 0).
  * No edges: universe_size = 0, which is yes for every k >= 0.
  * k >= n: all n vertex-sets together cover every edge, so the target is yes.
  * Vertices with no incident edges simply yield empty sets, which is allowed.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # One set per vertex; set[v] collects the indices of edges incident to v.
    sets = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for index, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
        sets[u].append(index)
        sets[v].append(index)

    return {"universe_size": len(edges), "sets": sets, "k": k}
EOF

- `universe_size = len(edges)` — each element corresponds to one edge.
- For each vertex `v`, create a set containing the indices of all edges incident to `v` (empty set if `v` is isolated).
- Keep the same `k`.

**Correctness:** A subset of vertices covers every edge iff the corresponding sets cover every element (edge index). Thus the minimum vertex cover size equals the minimum set cover size, so the yes/no answer is preserved for the same `k`.

- `k ≥ n`: all `n` vertex-sets cover the universe → yes.
- An element in no set would mean an edge with no endpoint, which can't happen for valid input.
